# Signalsmith dependencies

Signalsmith Linear is unmodified. Signalsmith Stretch contains YARG's transient protection and PVDR phase integration changes. PVDR is adapted from Holighaus and Průša, "Phase vocoder done right", Proc. EUSIPCO 2017, pp. 976–980. Both are built locally without network access or shared-library dependencies.

| Library | Version | Upstream commit | License |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Signalsmith Stretch](https://github.com/Signalsmith-Audio/signalsmith-stretch) | 1.3.2 | 57b93f4e9206a089a45387eaa39bdc9f310d3308 | [MIT](signalsmith-stretch/LICENSE.txt) |
| [Signalsmith Linear](https://github.com/Signalsmith-Audio/linear) | 0.3.1 | 5668673560146a9cfe38c25315071e3fd68c8317 | [MIT](signalsmith-linear/LICENSE.txt) |

Stretch requires Linear's `stft.h` and `fft.h`. Linear 0.3.1 is the dependency pinned by Stretch's upstream CMake configuration.

## YARG local patches to Stretch (`signalsmith-stretch/signalsmith-stretch.h`)

- Transient detection (`protectTransients`): high-frequency spectral flux over three bands above 1500 Hz (`setTransientFrequency`). Compares each bin with the maximum previous magnitude within three bins on either side, suppressing false attacks caused by pitch movement. Fires when a region exceeds absolute power, 0.3% of total power, and 25% filtered rising-energy ratio. Per-bin attack shaping retains its separate 45% unfiltered rising-energy threshold. Holds protection for half a block, then ignores new triggers for 1.5 blocks (~120ms) so decay bumps cannot machine-gun.
- Split-band diffusion: lows stay phase-coherent up to 6x stretch (`maxCleanLow`), so 20% speed stays clean for vocals and bass, while highs diffuse above 1x (`maxCleanHigh`, split at 0.11 of sample rate) to de-ring hats. Randomization is disabled while transient protection holds.
- Low-speed tonal neighbors: above 6x stretch, low bins preserve their phase difference from a processed parent when either bin exceeds the smoothed spectral background. This avoids randomizing the immediate neighbors of strong tones; bins without a strong neighbor retain diffusion.
- High-peak shelter (`PEAK_SHELTER_RADIUS`, `PEAK_SHELTER_RATIO`): strong high peaks shelter neighbors within four bins when the peak exceeds four times the smoothed background, so sustained high tones keep their skirts while true noise floor still diffuses.
- Extreme-stretch vertical lock (`VERTICAL_LOCK_MIN_STRETCH`): past 6x stretch, low bins inherit phase through the directly measured input ratio instead of the amplified frequency-direction gradient, whose estimate modulation otherwise dominates swept tones there. The gradient path stays for moderate stretch, where it measures better.
- Smoothed stretch factor (`TIMEFACTOR_SMOOTHING`, `TIMEFACTOR_SNAP_RATIO`): the per-spectrum input advance is fractional (89.6 samples at 20% speed) while sample positions are integers, so the measured factor alternates and wobbles every vertical twist. An exponential moving average (0.05) smooths the factor used for continuous twist magnitudes at slowdown; deviations above 10% snap through for real rate changes, regime decisions keep the raw factor, unity/fast paths are bit-identical, and the silence shortcut keeps tracking per-call ratios so the estimate never goes stale.
- Reassigned phase gradients: two extra analyses use the derivative of the analysis window and its centered time-weighted form. Their complex ratios with the ordinary spectrum estimate temporal and frequency-direction phase gradients. Temporal gradients are averaged across output frames; frequency gradients are averaged across parent/child bins before propagation. The existing half-bin rotation, pitch mapping, phase traversal, stereo reference and transient overrides remain in place. Both analyses use the existing processing-step schedule, restore the ordinary window after each step, and add no latency or callback allocations.
- Transient phase path: protected spectra bypass PVDR parent propagation and use vertical-only phase locking. PVDR traversal (`preparePvdrTraversal`) is adapted from Holighaus and Průša, "Phase vocoder done right", EUSIPCO 2017.
- Transient 1x stride (`src/stretch/StretchTempoStream.cpp`, `nextInputFrames`): protected blocks consume input at 1x while output positions still stretch, so transient magnitude is never dilated. The surplus/deficit accrues to `strideDebt_`, capped at 40ms of source audio to bound dense-mix drift while preserving isolated hits, and is repaid at up to 50% of nominal per block, preserving average tempo and exact `position()` history. Engages only for speeds 0.1–4x, only after a detected onset (`strideArmed`), and never on exhausted sources.
- Experiment flag (`stretchVariant_`, `pvdrSteer_`): `YARG_STRETCH_VARIANT` bits parsed once in `configure` select isolated phase/magnitude micro-variants for measurement (1 chirp-rate term, 2 heap steering, 4 time/frequency blend, 8 vortex routing, 16 gradient smoothing, 32 magnitude transport, 64 HF resynthesis, 128 valley freeze). Default 0 is bit-identical to the unflagged engine.

The onset neighborhood filter is an independent implementation of the maximum-filter idea in Böck and Widmer, ["Maximum Filter Vibrato Suppression for Onset Detection" (DAFx 2013)](https://www.cp.jku.at/research/papers/Boeck_Widmer_DAFx_2013.pdf), prompted by reviewing [Nanowarp's detector](https://github.com/neputevshina/nanowarp/blob/a462699e2b601122b342fc3e7e70d88ce4275bc1/detector.go). Nanowarp is Apache-2.0 licensed; its Go implementation is not included or linked. YARG uses the existing linear-frequency spectra and regional thresholds rather than Nanowarp's logarithmic frequency bands and offline onset curve.

The phase-gradient implementation was also prompted by [Nanowarp's reassignment-based warper](https://github.com/neputevshina/nanowarp/blob/a462699e2b601122b342fc3e7e70d88ce4275bc1/warper.go). Its signs, scaling and centered window origin were derived independently for Signalsmith's modified real FFT. YARG keeps its strongest-channel reference rather than forming a summed mono reference. It does not adopt Nanowarp's hard spectral-bin deletion or its offline time curve.
